summary: Implemented the accepted F4 mechanism (ADR-022 as amended by ADR-029), F6 excluded. (1) A single bounded, versioned, integrity-checked Cache-authority cursor record (fixed kind 'reconciliation-cursor', fixed id 'current') carrying only the sorted enabled-library set, the movie/episode surface scope, and the opaque (SortName, itemId) position; a missing/torn/out-of-bounds/scope-changed record resets to the start. (2) IWorkHintSink gains the bounded WorkHintEnqueueOutcome vocabulary (Accepted/Coalesced/InFlight/Overflow/Stopped) while the boolean TryEnqueue is retained for library events, webhooks, and the post-save trigger. (3) IMediaLibraryEnumerator gains an identity-anchored resume that walks the host-ordered pages in bounded ReconciliationBatchSize pages (cancellation between and inside pages, yields between pages), locates the unique itemId and returns the page beginning strictly after it, and reports an unlocatable anchor (no host after-key predicate is attempted). (4) LibraryReconciliationService advances the cursor for Scheduled/PostScan only: Accepted/Coalesced/InFlight and no-work items are covered and the run continues, Overflow/Stopped/fence/cancellation stop it with the cursor advanced only over the covered prefix, the end of the order wraps the cursor to the start, and PostSave still enumerates from the start and never reads or writes the cursor. interpretations.question: What exactly is the 'supported item-type scope' component of the ADR-022 clause 4 scope identity?
interpretations.chosen: The movie/episode badge-surface enablement (BadgeMoviePosters/BadgeEpisodePosters) of the snapshot that drives eligibility.
interpretations.basis: The candidate query is always Movie+Episode (fixed), so the only configurable item-type scope whose change can alter which candidates are reconciled is the two surface flags; ADR-022 clause 5 requires a reset when the item-type scope differs so a changed scope cannot leave the cursor past unenumerated items.
interpretations.impact: Enabling/disabling movie or episode posters resets the cursor to the start (a bounded re-cover). Persisted behaviour only; no user-visible configuration change.

interpretations.question: Does the identity-anchored resume return the page after the anchor's page (page-aligned) or the page beginning at the anchor's absolute index + 1 (strictly after the located item)?
interpretations.chosen: The page begins at the located anchor item's absolute index + 1 (items strictly after the anchor), implemented through the supported StartIndex/Limit offset paging.
interpretations.basis: ADR-022 clause 3 requires the resume to return the page strictly after a supplied key and clause 2 requires the next run to resume at the first uncovered (overflowed) item; ADR-029 clause 2's 'returns the page strictly after it' refers to the located boundary item. A page-aligned return would skip the anchor page's tail for a cycle.
interpretations.impact: No strictly ordered item is deferred a cycle by the resume granularity; the locate walk remains O(offset) rows in bounded pages.

interpretations.question: How does the bounded outcome vocabulary classify a malformed hint (an empty item id or a default LibraryWorkItem), which the ADR does not define?
interpretations.basis: The vocabulary is fixed at five values; a malformed hint can never be queued, and the stop classification makes a whole-scope run stop at it rather than silently skip unqueueable work. The reconciliation service never emits such a hint (it skips Guid.Empty and non-eligible items before the enqueue boundary), so this only guards a programming error.
interpretations.impact: Unreachable from the documented whole-scope path; boolean TryEnqueue still returns false for the same input as before.

interpretations.question: How are the new bounded enqueue outcomes mapped onto the run result, which previously had no overflow vocabulary?
interpretations.chosen: Overflow maps to a new bounded LibraryReconciliationOutcome.QueueSaturated (the run stopped at the bounded queue capacity); Stopped maps to the existing Fenced outcome (the ADR defines Stopped as the lifecycle fence being raised or the plugin shutting down). Both stop the run and advance the cursor only over the covered prefix.
interpretations.basis: ADR-022 clause 2 describes Overflow and Stopped identically for cursor advancement but does not name a run result; the existing Fenced value already means 'the lifecycle fence refused new work'.
interpretations.impact: A bounded diagnostic value is added to the run outcome; the log event selection for it remains ReconciliationSkipped and carries the bounded reason text.

interpretations.question: Does the post-save prefix re-cover stop at the first Overflow like the cursor-governed runs?
interpretations.chosen: No: PostSave keeps the pre-F4 behavior (enumerate the whole scope, enqueue what fits, Completed outcome) and never reads or writes the cursor.
interpretations.basis: ADR-022 clause 6 states the bounded post-save trigger is deliberately excluded, always enumerates from the start, and leaves the cursor untouched; the per-run stop rule is the cursor advance rule of clause 2.
interpretations.impact: Post-save Inspected/Eligible/Enqueued counts and its Completed outcome are unchanged from before this task; only the scheduled/post-scan runs stop at the first overflow.

interpretations.question: What happens when the cursor record or the host SortName hint cannot be read at runtime?
interpretations.chosen: The cursor read/write is best-effort (a read failure is a miss and resets to the start; a write failure leaves the previous record and never fails the run), and a SortName hint that cannot be read is stored as an empty hint while the unique itemId remains the anchor.
interpretations.basis: The cursor is rebuildable Cache state (ADR-022 clause 4) and ADR-029 clause 3 makes the SortName component a boundary hint/diagnostic, not the ordering authority.
interpretations.impact: A state or hint failure degrades the mechanism to a bounded re-cover or a lossless identity anchor; no run result changes.
